answer: Reputation decays with an exponential half-life, so past trust fades unless an identity sustains honest service. In the EigenTrust kernel, centrality flows through reciprocal, credible endorsements; a fresh sybil has almost no trusted incoming mass, and its weak ripple through the river of transitive links leaves eigenvector centrality near zero. New identities cannot manufacture that history or pass consensus without prolonged, verifiable contribution.
